question.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that its augmented matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

 

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\  & =2(\frac{3}{2}{x}_{3})+3{x}_{3} \\  & =6{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}6{x}_{3} \\ \frac{3}{2}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=2,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
